correctness.rationale: Chain-rule factorization is exact; a real Rolle argument (using \(u^{r/d}Q(u)\)) counts every reduced root and proves simplicity in \((0,1)\), positivity and no zero at \(u=0\); the endpoint recurrence decreases multiplicity to zero at \(m=n\) and prevents new endpoint roots for \(m>n\). The normalized descendant has the declared degree, leaving no unaccounted roots. Every finite zero is consequently on the star. Theorem 1.4(i) of arXiv:2610.09602v1 supplies K connected and containing all vertices; unique arcs in the star force the reverse inclusion. Exact symbolic tests cover 567 instances, not an infinite proof. Risk: relies on the cited general connected-core theorem.

value.rationale: Regular root polygons are a canonical excluded symmetry case of the earlier generic descendant discussion and a natural stress test for the newly defined full shadow. The theorem completely classifies a nontrivial infinite family in every d>=3, all powers and derivative orders, with exact radial zero counts, a one-dimensional core despite a two-dimensional convex hull, and complete absence of transients contrasted with the recent quartic examples. It gives a useful baseline for geometric and perturbative studies; it does not assert a general stability or density formula.
